item.title: A Hybrid ML and Rule-Based Approach to SQL Backup Monitoring
item.content:encoded: This article presents a hybrid approach to SQL Server backup monitoring that combines telemetry collection, statistical anomaly detection, and rule-based alerting to identify performance drift before backups begin failing outright. Using a lightweight telemetry table, rolling operational metrics, Isolation Forest models, and recoverability checks like LSN chain validation, the piece demonstrates how backup systems can be monitored as evolving operational behaviors rather than simple binary success events.

item.title: Your AI Agent Processed That Invoice. So Did the Attacker
item.content:encoded: Using a real reimbursement automation workflow as a case study, this article examines how prompt injection attacks in agentic AI systems can lead to silent, continuous data exfiltration without triggering obvious failures. Rather than framing the issue as a model defect, it argues that the core problem is architectural: most AI pipelines fail to separate external data from trusted instructions. The piece connects modern agentic vulnerabilities to classic security concepts like the confused deputy problem and outlines why provenance-aware authorization, runtime policy enforcement, and stricter trust boundaries are becoming essential for production AI systems.

item.title: A Case Study on How PHP Handles Identifiers and Text Internally

item.title: The Mathematical Foundations of Zero-Knowledge Proofs
item.content:encoded: This article is a deep technical exploration of zero-knowledge proof systems and the mathematical foundations behind modern blockchain scaling infrastructure. The piece then connects these ideas to practical rollup architectures like zkEVMs and compares the engineering tradeoffs between SNARK and STARK systems in terms of proof size, proving complexity, trusted setups, and on-chain verification costs.

The fix is to model ClamAV's three real outcomes — Clean, Malicious, ScanError — as three explicit return values, and force the caller to handle ScanError as a security decision rather than a programming error.
